title: Advent of the English East India Company

notes.subtopic: 1. Big Picture — From Traders to Rulers
notes.content:
**Executive summary:** The British came to India as **traders** and became **rulers** by defeating Indian rulers (Bengal, Awadh, Mysore…) and their biggest European rival, the **French**. Three **Carnatic Wars (1746–1763)** gave the EEIC control of **southern India**.

**Carnatic coast:** region between the **Eastern Ghats** and the **Coromandel Coast** — modern Tamil Nadu, south-east Karnataka, south Andhra Pradesh.

**Chapter map:** EEIC's arrival → French Company → Carnatic Wars I, II, III → Reasons for British success → Lessons learnt.

fiveW.who: British merchants; Queen Elizabeth I; Thomas Roe; Jahangir
fiveW.where: Surat, Ahmedabad, Agra, Broach, Masulipatnam; Madras, Bombay, Calcutta
fiveW.what: A private trading company that set up factories and presidencies
fiveW.how: Royal charter for exclusive trade; concessions from the Mughals; fortified posts

notes.content:
• **1600** — private company of British merchants; got the **exclusive right to trade in the East** from **Queen Elizabeth I** (who took a share of profits).
• **1615** — **Sir Thomas Roe** at **Jahangir's** court → many concessions.
• **By 1623** — factories at **Surat, Ahmedabad, Agra, Broach, Masulipatnam**.
• **1639** — **Madras** given by a local ruler → **Fort St George** (first English fortress, founded 1644).
• **Bombay** — wedding gift to **King Charles II** on marrying Portuguese princess **Catherine of Braganza**; he gave it to the Company (1668).
• **End of 17th century** — **Fort William**, Calcutta.
• **Three Presidencies** — **Madras, Bombay, Calcutta**, each under a **Governor**.

**Factory** = a trading post (warehouse/office).

notes.subtopic: 3. French East India Company and the Rivalry
notes.content:
• **French East India Company formed in 1664**; headquarters **Pondicherry** (Puducherry); settlements at **Mahe** and **Chandernagore**.
• By the 18th century the **Dutch and Portuguese** lost their posts → **Britain and France** were the two big powers left.
• Contest for **trade monopoly** and **colonies** → the **Carnatic Wars**.
• Indian rulers took the side of the British or French to win their own **wars of succession**.
• Britain and France were **rivals in Europe** too — European wars spilled over into India.

fiveW.who: French Governor Joseph Dupleix vs the British; Anwaruddin Khan, Nawab of Carnatic
fiveW.why: War of Austrian Succession (1740) in Europe — Britain and France on opposite sides
fiveW.how: Dupleix captured Madras, defeated the Nawab's army; the European treaty restored Madras

notes.content:
• **Cause:** the **War of Austrian Succession** (1740–48) in Europe.
• **Joseph Dupleix**, French Governor, wanted **French supremacy**; **captured Madras**.
• He refused to hand over Fort St George to **Anwaruddin Khan, Nawab of Carnatic**; the Nawab's army was **defeated by the French**.
• War in Europe ended in **1748** (**Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle**) → **Madras returned** to the British.

**Results**
• **No territorial gains** for either side.
• **Prestige of the French increased** — a small European force had beaten a large Indian army.

fiveW.who: Dupleix vs Robert Clive; rival claimants in the Carnatic
fiveW.what: Anglo-French war through local succession disputes
fiveW.why: Dupleix's ambition to gain more territory
fiveW.how: The French backed one claimant and the British another; Clive defeated the French

notes.content:
• **Cause:** Dupleix's ambition — he interfered in **regional succession rivalries** (e.g. backed **Muzaffar Jang**, grandson of Nizam-ul-Mulk).
• **Robert Clive**, then a **young clerk** of the EEIC, **defeated the French**.
• **Muhammad Ali**, son of Anwaruddin, made **Nawab of Carnatic** by the British.
• Ended with the **Treaty of Pondicherry (1754)**.

**Results**
• British power and prestige in the Carnatic **restored**.
• **Dupleix recalled** to France.

fiveW.what: Final Anglo-French war — French completely defeated
fiveW.how: Funds from Bengal after Plassey (1757) and naval supremacy; victory at Wandiwash

notes.content:
• **Cause:** the **Seven Years' War (1756–63)** in Europe (England vs France; also Austria, Spain, Russia, Prussia, Portugal).
• Coincided with the **Battle of Plassey (1757)** — control of **Bengal gave the British funds** to fight the French.
• **Battle of Wandiwash (1760)** — French **completely defeated**.
• Ended with the **Treaty of Paris (1763)**.

**Results:** British became the **dominant European power in south India**; French confined to trade (Pondicherry etc.).

• **Naval supremacy** — British navy far superior.
• **Steady supply** of arms and resources from the naval base at **Bombay**.
• **Financial stability** — land revenue of **Bengal** after 1757.
• **EEIC was a private concern** — free from government interference; the **French Company was controlled by the French government** and could not take major decisions on its own.

**Lessons the British learnt**
• **Quarrels among Indian rulers** could be used to gain control.
• Large, **old-fashioned Indian armies** were no match for trained European armies.
• **Indian soldiers (sepoys)** could be recruited and trained **cheaply** → a large army of Indian sepoys under British officers → **paramount power** in India.

questions.question: Which statements are true? (i) The Carnatic coast lies between the Western Ghats and the Coromandel Coast (ii) Three presidencies were at Madras, Bombay, Calcutta (iii) Pondicherry was the French HQ
questions.answer: **ii and iii.** The Carnatic lies between the **Eastern** Ghats and the Coromandel Coast.

questions.question: Answer briefly: (a) When did the EEIC get its charter? (b) Who received Bombay as a wedding gift? (c) Where was the French HQ? (d) Name the first English fortress in India.
questions.answer:
• (a) 1600, from Queen Elizabeth I.
  • (b) King Charles II of England, on marrying Catherine of Braganza.
  • (c) Pondicherry (Puducherry).
  • (d) Fort St George, Madras (1644).

questions.question: Trace the growth of the EEIC in India up to the end of the 17th century.
questions.answer:
• 1600 — royal charter from Elizabeth I for exclusive trade in the East.
  • 1615 — Thomas Roe won concessions from Jahangir; by 1623 factories at Surat, Ahmedabad, Agra, Broach, Masulipatnam.
  • 1639 — Madras → Fort St George.
  • Bombay — from Charles II (wedding gift).
  • End of 17th century — Fort William, Calcutta; three Presidencies under Governors.

questions.question: Describe the First Carnatic War — its cause, events and results.
questions.answer:
• Cause: the War of Austrian Succession in Europe, with Britain and France on opposite sides.
  • Events: Dupleix captured Madras; refused to hand it to Anwaruddin Khan, whose army was defeated by the French.
  • End: European treaty of 1748 — Madras returned.
  • Results: no territorial gains; French prestige enhanced.
questions.topperTip: For each Carnatic War use the same 4 headings: Cause / Events / End / Results.

questions.question: (Picture) Identify the French Governor. Which British stronghold did he capture? What happened to him after the Second Carnatic War?
questions.answer:
• 1. Joseph Dupleix.
  • 2. Madras (First Carnatic War).
  • 3. He was recalled to France.

questions.question: What led to the Second Carnatic War? What were its results?
questions.answer:
• Cause: Dupleix's ambition for more territory — he involved the French army in regional succession rivalries in the Carnatic.
  • Robert Clive, a young EEIC clerk, defeated the French; Muhammad Ali became Nawab of Carnatic.
  • Results: British prestige restored; Dupleix recalled.

questions.question: What was the Seven Years' War? Why did the Third Carnatic War take place? How did the Carnatic Wars affect French plans?
questions.answer:
• Seven Years' War (1756–63): European war between England and France (with Austria, Spain, Russia, Prussia, Portugal); ended by the Treaty of Paris, 1763.
  • It broke the peace in India → Third Carnatic War.
  • The French were completely defeated at Wandiwash (1760); their dream of an Indian empire ended; the British became dominant in south India.

questions.question: How did hostility in Europe contribute to the Carnatic Wars, and how did the wars help the EEIC control most of India?
questions.answer:
• Europe → India: the War of Austrian Succession caused the First, and the Seven Years' War caused the Third Carnatic War — rivals in Europe fought in India too.
  • Gains for the EEIC: French power destroyed; British dominance in south India; they learnt to exploit quarrels among Indian rulers, saw that old Indian armies were weak, and built a cheap sepoy army — which helped them conquer most of India.

questions.question: State the reasons for the British success against the French in India.
questions.answer:
• Naval supremacy.
  • Steady supply of arms and resources from Bombay.
  • Financial stability from Bengal's revenue after Plassey.
  • EEIC was a private company, free from government interference, while the French Company depended on its government.

questions.question: Did French government interference affect French expansion in India? What gave the EEIC an edge?
questions.answer: Yes. The French Company could not take major political or military decisions without government consent, so it was slow and inflexible; its leaders like Dupleix were even recalled. The EEIC, a private concern, could act quickly, was backed by a superior navy and the wealth of Bengal.
